# Boldteq Marketing Site — Webflow → Next.js Conversion (Phase 1: Homepage)

## Context

The current Boldteq marketing site lives in Webflow with self-hosted Directus attached for CMS content (blog, case studies, etc.). We're migrating the full site to **Stack A** (Next.js 16.2.3 + React 19 + TypeScript strict + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui) hosted on Railway, alongside the existing self-hosted Directus instance (private networking, single platform).

**Why now:**
- Webflow is a rental — we don't own the code, can't version control, can't integrate deeply with our agent pipeline, and premium marketing perf (Core Web Vitals, edge caching, dynamic personalization) is capped by Webflow's runtime.
- Directus is already our content source of truth. Next.js lets us query it directly (SSG/ISR) without the Webflow middleman.
- This becomes the canonical Boldteq front door — the factory showcase — so it must be production-grade, fast, and SEO-perfect from day 1.

**Phase 1 scope (this plan):** Homepage ONLY. Fully static, design-inspired rebuild from the Webflow original, no Directus integration. Future phases add blog, case studies, and CMS-driven sections wired to Directus.

**Fidelity target:** Design-inspired — Vega reviews Webflow visual language and rebuilds cleanly in shadcn/Tailwind. Small improvements allowed; not a pixel-perfect clone.

---

## Decisions (locked)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Stack | Stack A — Next.js 16.2.3 App Router, React 19, TS strict, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, pnpm, Node 20 |
| Hosting | Railway (same platform as Directus → private networking later) |
| Phase 1 scope | Homepage only, fully static, no CMS |
| Directus role in Phase 1 | None. Phase 2+ for blog/case studies/CMS sections |
| Design fidelity | Design-inspired (Vega-led), not pixel-perfect |
| Fonts | Match Webflow fonts via `next/font` (self-hosted or Google) |
| Analytics | PostHog from day 1 |
| Error tracking | Sentry from day 1 |
| SEO | Metadata API, sitemap.ts, robots.ts, structured data (Organization + WebSite JSON-LD) |
| i18n | Not in Phase 1 |

---

## Agent Pipeline (BUILD Mode via Rex)

Rex orchestrates. Order of operations:

1. **Nova** — Scrape the live Webflow homepage: sections, copy, fonts, colors, imagery, CTAs, animations. Produce a component inventory + asset list.
2. **Vega** — Design spec for the Next.js homepage. Pulls Webflow screenshots, maps each section to shadcn primitives, defines layout grid, typography scale, color tokens, spacing rhythm, animation pattern (Framer Motion), dark mode stance, responsive breakpoints. Output: design spec doc + section-by-section component map.
3. **Arya** — Tiny architecture note: folder layout, env var list, asset pipeline, image optimization strategy (`next/image` + Directus passthrough for Phase 2), Railway service config. No DB needed for Phase 1.
4. **Riko** — Scaffold Stack A project in `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Boldteq`:
   - `pnpm create next-app@latest` → Next 16.2.3, TS strict, Tailwind 4, App Router, `src/` dir, ESLint
   - Install: shadcn/ui, framer-motion, lucide-react, zod, @sentry/nextjs, posthog-js, posthog-node
   - Configure: `tsconfig.json` strict, `eslint.config.mjs` (no-any rule), `.env.example`, `.env.local`, Railway service file (`railway.json`), GitHub repo + initial commit
   - Setup: Sentry init, PostHog provider, shadcn init, `app/layout.tsx` with font loading + metadata base, `app/robots.ts`, `app/sitemap.ts`
5. **Koda** — Build homepage sections per Vega's spec:
   - `app/page.tsx` — compose sections
   - `src/components/marketing/hero.tsx`
   - `src/components/marketing/features.tsx` (or whatever sections Vega maps)
   - `src/components/marketing/social-proof.tsx`
   - `src/components/marketing/cta.tsx`
   - `src/components/layout/site-header.tsx`
   - `src/components/layout/site-footer.tsx`
   - All server components by default; client only where interaction needed (mobile nav, animations)
   - Images via `next/image` with explicit width/height, AVIF/WebP
   - No `any`, no `console.log`, full a11y (semantic HTML, aria labels, alt text)
6. **Quill** — Refine homepage copy. Pull current Webflow copy as starting point, rewrite with Boldteq voice (software factory positioning, AI-first velocity, production-grade output). Every H1/H2/CTA earns its place.
7. **Zeph** — Technical SEO audit: metadata, Open Graph, Twitter cards, JSON-LD (Organization + WebSite with SearchAction), canonical URLs, sitemap, robots, Core Web Vitals check. Fixes in place before merge.
8. **Luna** — Playwright smoke tests: homepage loads, all CTAs render, no console errors, Lighthouse score ≥95 on Performance/SEO/A11y/Best Practices, mobile + desktop viewports.
9. **Sage** — Code review gate: TypeScript strict, no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`, Tailwind class hygiene, component size, bundle check, security headers, image optimization, a11y audit. Blocks deploy on critical findings.
10. **Bolt** — Deploy to Railway:
    - Create Railway project + service
    - Wire env vars (SENTRY_DSN, POSTHOG_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_* etc.)
    - Connect custom domain (TBD — need from Yash)
    - Preview deployment first, then promote to production
    - Smoke tests on deployed URL
11. **Hawk** — Post-deploy monitoring setup: Sentry alerts, Railway health checks, PostHog activation event (page view on `/`), uptime monitor.
12. **Mira** — Extract lessons, update `~/.claude/memory/projects/boldteq-marketing.md` and stack file if any new patterns emerge.

---

│   │       └── cta.tsx
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── utils.ts
│   │   ├── seo.ts                 ← metadata helpers
│   │   └── analytics.ts           ← PostHog wrapper
│   └── config/
│       └── site.ts                ← site name, URL, nav links
├── public/
│   └── (brand assets from Webflow export)
├── .env.example
├── .env.local
├── next.config.ts
├── tailwind.config.ts (or v4 inline)
├── tsconfig.json                  ← strict
├── eslint.config.mjs
├── railway.json
├── package.json
└── CLAUDE.md                      ← project memory
```

---

## Critical Files to Create

- [src/app/page.tsx](src/app/page.tsx) — homepage composition
- [src/app/layout.tsx](src/app/layout.tsx) — root layout, fonts, metadata base, PostHog + Sentry providers
- [src/lib/seo.ts](src/lib/seo.ts) — `buildMetadata()` helper with OG, Twitter, canonical
- [src/app/sitemap.ts](src/app/sitemap.ts) — dynamic sitemap (homepage only for now, extensible)
- [src/app/robots.ts](src/app/robots.ts)
- [src/config/site.ts](src/config/site.ts) — single source of truth for site name/URL/nav
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) — project rules, Directus connection info for Phase 2, forbidden patterns

---

## What I Need From Yash Before Execution

1. **Webflow homepage URL** (live site or `*.webflow.io` staging) — Nova needs it for scraping.
2. **Custom domain** for the new Next.js site — Bolt needs it for Railway DNS.
3. **Directus base URL** (even though Phase 1 doesn't use it — Arya will document it in CLAUDE.md for Phase 2).
4. **Sentry project** access (create new or use existing Boldteq org).
5. **PostHog project** access (same — new or existing).
6. **GitHub repo** — create `boldteq-marketing` or similar, or let Riko create it.
7. **Brand assets** — if Webflow has custom fonts/logos not publicly downloadable, provide them.

---

## Verification

Before declaring Phase 1 done:

1. `pnpm dev` → homepage renders locally at `http://localhost:3000`, no console errors, all sections visible, responsive down to 375px.
2. `pnpm build` → clean build, no TS errors, no ESLint errors, no `any` usage.
3. `pnpm lint` → passes.
4. Playwright smoke suite (Luna) → all green.
5. Lighthouse on preview deploy → Performance ≥95, SEO 100, A11y ≥95, Best Practices 100.
6. Sage review → zero critical findings.
7. Deployed preview URL loads, `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` return correctly, structured data validates in Google Rich Results Test.
8. Sentry receives a test error; PostHog receives the pageview.
9. Mobile viewport check on real device (iOS Safari + Android Chrome).

---

## Phase 2+ (NOT in this plan, noted for continuity)

- Directus TypeScript SDK + typed collection helpers
- Blog: `app/blog/page.tsx` + `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` with ISR (`revalidate: 60`)
- Case studies: same pattern
- CMS-driven homepage sections (optional — if we want marketing to edit hero copy without deploys)
- Directus image proxy through `next/image` with allowed domain config
- Webhook from Directus → Next.js on-demand revalidation (`revalidateTag`)
- Multi-language support if needed

Phase 2 will get its own plan file after Phase 1 ships.

## What a "dataset" is in Sanity

A **dataset** = an isolated content store inside a Sanity project. Think of it as a database environment, not a workspace for a different app.

```
Sanity Project: "boldteq-marketing"
├── dataset: production   ← live blog posts your site reads
└── dataset: staging      ← drafts, schema tests, sandbox

Sanity Project: "pinzo-marketing"   ← completely separate project
├── dataset: production
└── dataset: staging
```

Each dataset:
- Has its own documents, assets, and history
- Can be public (read without token) or private (token required)
- Is queried by name: `client.fetch(query, {}, { dataset: 'production' })`
- Shares the project's schema definitions (so `production` and `staging` have the same content types)

**Key point:** datasets do NOT separate different apps. You separate apps by creating different **projects**. Each project gets its own 2 datasets on free tier.

## Is 2 datasets enough for blog-only?

**Yes — 2 is actually more than most blog sites need.** Here's the standard pattern:

| Dataset | Purpose | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| `production` | Live content your marketing site reads | ✅ Always |
| `staging` (or `development`) | Test schema changes, preview new post types before pushing live | Optional — only if you change schemas often |

For "just blog posts, nothing more," **you realistically only use 1 dataset** (`production`). The second slot sits unused unless you want a sandbox to experiment in.

## Your actual Sanity setup for 10 apps

```
boldteq-marketing      → production (1 of 2 used)
pinzo-marketing        → production (1 of 2 used)
rankora-marketing      → production (1 of 2 used)
crobot-marketing       → production (1 of 2 used)
storelocator-marketing → production (1 of 2 used)
sizechart-marketing    → production (1 of 2 used)
app7-marketing         → production (1 of 2 used)
app8-marketing         → production (1 of 2 used)
app9-marketing         → production (1 of 2 used)
app10-marketing        → production (1 of 2 used)

Total: 10 projects, 10 datasets used, 10 free slots unused.
Cost: $0.
```

**The 2-dataset limit will never bind for blog-only use.** It only matters if someone is running, say, a production blog + a preview blog + an archive blog + a translated-content blog all in one project — that's when 2 becomes tight.

## Where the free tier CAN bind (even for blog-only)

The dataset count is a non-issue. The real gotchas remain:

| Limit | Blog-only risk |
|---|---|
| **3 users per project** | If your marketing team grows past 3 editors per site, $15/user/mo |
| **10 GB bandwidth/project/mo** | One viral blog post with unoptimized hero images can burn this. Next.js ISR + `next/image` optimization eliminates most of the risk |
| **500K CDN requests** | Next.js ISR caches these — you'd need an extremely busy blog to hit it |
| **5 GB asset storage** | ~500–1000 blog post cover images before it matters |

**For a blog-only × 10 apps scenario, the datasets are not your problem.** The users-per-project cap is the only realistic risk, and only if your team grows.

---

## Bottom line

- **Datasets are irrelevant to your decision.** 2 is plenty for blog-only. This is not a limit you'll ever hit.
- **Sanity free tier is genuinely workable for 10 blog-only marketing sites** *if* you stay solo or small team (≤3 editors per project) and never add a credit card.
- **But the "$0 forever" guarantee only exists with Keystatic or MDX files.** Sanity can change its free tier anytime — you'd be betting on their pricing page staying generous for years.

My recommendation stands: **Keystatic for pure blog-only × 10 apps.** But if you strongly prefer Sanity's editor UX and accept the vendor risk, the dataset limit is not a reason to say no.

All 3 seats can edit the SAME post at the SAME time.

Sanity's architecture works **in your favor** at factory scale. Here's why:

Every Sanity project is a separate billing unit. The free tier seat cap resets per project.

Project 2 (pinzo):        fresh free seats

### 2. API tokens don't consume seats

This is the most important rule for an AI-first factory:

```
Your agents (Koda, Quill, Luna, Mira) write via API tokens
→ 0 seats consumed
→ Unlimited posts, unlimited projects

Humans who log into Studio UI consume seats
→ Only count real people with web logins
```

For a Boldteq factory where **Quill writes 90%+ of blog posts automatically**, most projects will have exactly **1 human seat (you)** — leaving multiple free seats per project permanently unused.

|---|---|---|---|---|

- Existing projects have historically been grandfathered for a period when free tiers contracted
- Competitors exist and a migration is a weekend, not a year

**Important: my earlier numbers were wrong.** The live pricing page shows much more generous limits than I stated. Let me correct everything with verified numbers.

## Sanity Free Plan — real limits (verified April 2026)

These are **per project**. Each of your 25 apps gets its own full allocation independently.

| Resource | Free plan (per project) | Your usage (blog-only, 1-2 editors) | Safe? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User seats** | **20** | 1–2 | ✅ Massive headroom |
| **Datasets** | 2 (public only) | 1 (production) | ✅ |
| **Documents** | 10,000 | ~50–300 blog posts over years | ✅ |
| **API CDN requests** | 1,000,000 / month | Near zero with Next.js ISR | ✅ |
| **API requests** | 250,000 / month | Studio edits + webhook fires | ✅ |
| **Asset storage** | 100 GB | ~5,000 cover images at 20MB each | ✅ |
| **Bandwidth** | 100 GB / month | Near zero with next/image caching | ✅ |
| **Webhooks** | 2 | 1 for Next.js revalidation | ✅ |
| **Live connections** | 1,000 per dataset | Studio real-time sync | ✅ |
| **Overages** | **Blocked, not billed** | Can't accidentally spend money | ✅ |
| **Credit card required** | No | — | ✅ |

## Your 25-app factory math

Since limits are per-project, you get the full free allocation × 25:

```
25 projects × 20 seats each     =  500 total seat slots (you'll use 25–50)
25 projects × 10K docs each     =  250,000 total documents
25 projects × 100 GB bandwidth  =  2.5 TB total bandwidth/month
25 projects × 100 GB storage    =  2.5 TB total asset storage
25 projects × 1M CDN requests   =  25M CDN requests/month
```

**For blog-only content, you will never come close to any of these limits on free tier.** Not even remotely.

## What's NOT included on free (the real trade-offs)

This is where it gets honest. Free gives you generous quotas but locks certain **features** behind the Growth plan ($15/seat/month):

| Feature | Free plan | Growth plan ($15/seat/mo) | Does it matter for you? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Permission roles** | Only **Admin + Viewer** | Admin, Editor, Developer, Contributor, Viewer | ⚠️ **Both your editors will be full Admins** — can change schemas, delete collections, modify settings. Fine for trusted people (you + 1), risky if you hire an unknown freelancer |
| **Scheduled publishing** | ❌ Not available | ✅ Schedule posts for future dates | ⚠️ **You can't write a post today and schedule it for next Tuesday.** You'd publish manually or build a workaround via cron |
| **Comments & Tasks** | ❌ Not available | ✅ Built-in editorial workflow | Minor — you don't need editorial approval for 1-2 person teams |
| **AI Assist** | ❌ Not available | ✅ Built-in AI writing help | Irrelevant — Quill is your AI writer |
| **Private datasets** | ❌ Public only | ✅ Private or public | ⚠️ **Your blog content is publicly queryable by anyone who knows your project ID.** For a marketing blog this is fine — it's public content anyway. But don't put anything sensitive in Sanity |
| **Extra datasets** | Can't buy more | $999/dataset/mo (!) | Irrelevant — you'll use 1 of 2 |

## Realistic cost breakdown for 25 apps

### Scenario 1: All 25 apps stay on free (most likely)

```
Monthly cost:  $0
Annual cost:   $0
3-year cost:   $0
```

**This works if:** both editors per project are trusted admins, you don't need scheduled publishing, and you're OK with public datasets. For blog-only marketing sites with 1-2 trusted editors, this is the expected path.

### Scenario 2: 2-3 flagship apps upgrade to Growth (moderate scenario)

Say Boldteq's own marketing site + 2 top apps need scheduled publishing or editorial roles:

```
3 projects × 2 seats × $15/seat/mo = $90/month
22 projects stay free               = $0

Monthly cost:  $90
Annual cost:   $1,080
3-year cost:   $3,240
```

### Scenario 3: You hit a document or bandwidth limit on one project (unlikely for blog)

You can't go over — Sanity blocks new content instead of billing. So the cost is $0, but you'd need to:
- Delete old drafts to free document slots, OR
- Upgrade that one project to Growth ($15/seat/mo, which gives 25K docs)

```
1 project upgraded × 2 seats × $15 = $30/month
Everything else free                = $0

Monthly cost:  $30
```

### Scenario 4: Absolute worst case (all 25 need Growth)

Every project hits a limit or needs editorial workflows:

```
25 projects × 2 seats × $15 = $750/month
Annual:  $9,000
3-year:  $27,000
```

**This is extremely unlikely for blog-only content.** I include it only for completeness.

## Growth plan overage costs (if you ever upgrade)

If a project IS on Growth and exceeds included quotas, these kick in:

| Overage | Cost |
|---|---|
| Additional documents (up to 50K total) | $299 flat |
| API CDN requests above 1M | $1 per 250K |
| API requests above 250K | $1 per 25K |
| Extra storage above 100 GB | $0.50 per GB |
| Extra bandwidth above 100 GB | $0.30 per GB |
| Additional datasets | $999/dataset/month (!) |

**Never buy extra datasets.** $999/mo is insane. If you need a 3rd dataset, create a new project instead (free).

## The 2 things I was wrong about earlier

| What I said | Reality | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| "3 user seats on free" | **20 seats on free** | Much better — seat limit is a non-issue |
| "1 dataset on free" (in one response) | **2 datasets on free** | You get production + staging |

The free tier is far more generous than I initially stated. The real limitation is **feature gating** (roles, scheduling), not quotas.

## My updated honest recommendation

For **25 apps, blog-only, 1-2 editors per app:**

| Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **CMS** | Sanity, free plan for all 25 apps |
| **Expected cost** | $0/month for 22–25 apps, possibly $30–90/mo for 1–3 flagship apps if you want scheduled publishing or editor roles |
| **Biggest gotcha** | Both editors are full Admins on free — keep Sanity login to trusted people only |
| **Second gotcha** | Public datasets — don't put anything non-public in Sanity (blog content is public anyway, so fine) |
| **Backup strategy** | Nightly `sanity dataset export` → GitHub repo (free, removes vendor risk) |
| **When to upgrade a project** | Only when that specific project needs scheduled publishing, editorial roles, or private datasets |

**Bottom line: $0/month for your entire 25-app factory is realistic and sustainable for blog-only use, with the nightly backup escape hatch in place.**

Here's the honest answer: **No CMS provider offers a true "one plan covers all projects" model.** Every major headless CMS bills per project/space/site. But the costs are wildly different. Here's the full comparison for your exact use case: **25 apps, blog-only, 1-2 editors each.**

## Head-to-head: 25 apps, blog-only, 1-2 editors

### Sanity

```
Free plan: unlimited projects, each gets full free tier independently
25 apps × $0 = $0/month

If 3 apps later need Growth: 3 × 2 seats × $15 = $90/mo
```

| | Free (per project) |
|---|---|
| Projects | **Unlimited** |
| Seats | 20 |
| Documents | 10,000 |
| API CDN requests | 1,000,000/mo |
| Bandwidth | 100 GB/mo |
| Storage | 100 GB |
| Roles | Admin + Viewer only |
| Billing model | Per project, independently |

**25-app cost: $0/mo**

---

### ButterCMS

```
Free plan: 50 blog posts limit — that's it, 50 posts total per site
Even 1 serious blog needs the $71/mo Basic plan (100 posts)
25 apps × $71 = $1,775/month
```

| | Free | Basic |
|---|---|---|
| Projects per plan | 1 | 1 |
| Blog posts | **50** | 100 |
| API calls | 50K/mo | 100K/mo |
| Users | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Roles | 2 | 2 |

**Pro:** Unlimited users on every plan (no seat billing).
**Con:** 50 blog post cap on free is useless. Per-site billing makes 25 apps impossibly expensive.

**25-app cost: $1,775/mo** (Basic) or **$0 if you never exceed 50 posts per site** (but you will)

---

### Storyblok

```
Free plan: 1 space, 1 user only — can't even add a second editor
Growth plan: $99/mo per space
25 apps × $99 = $2,475/month
```

| | Free | Growth |
|---|---|---|
| Spaces (projects) | 1 | 1 |
| Users | **1** | 5 |
| Stories (content) | 20,000 | 25,000 |
| API requests | 100K/mo | 1M/mo |

**Pro:** Excellent visual editor, great for marketing pages.
**Con:** 1 user on free is deal-breaking. Per-space billing at $99 makes 25 apps insane.

**25-app cost: $2,475/mo**

---

### DatoCMS

```
Free plan: 3 projects max, 300 records (!) — barely enough for 10 blog posts with images
Professional: €199/mo + €39/mo per extra project
25 apps = €199 + (24 × €39) = €1,135/month
```

| | Free | Professional |
|---|---|---|
| Projects | **3 max** | 1 included + extras at €39/mo each |
| Editors | 1 | 10 |
| Records (documents) | **300** | 100,000 |
| Bandwidth | 10 GB/mo | 1 TB/mo |
| API calls | 100K/mo | 1M/mo |

**Pro:** Closest to "shared billing" — one account, add projects for €39 each.
**Con:** 300 records on free is a joke. €39/project/mo adds up fast. And the Professional base price is €199/mo before adding any extra projects.

**25-app cost: €1,135/mo ($1,250+)**

---

### Directus (self-hosted on Coolify)

```
Free open-source, one instance per app on a VPS
25 instances on Hetzner CX32 (€8/mo) or CX42 (€16/mo)
```

| | Self-hosted |
|---|---|
| Projects | Unlimited (one instance each) |
| Users | Unlimited |
| Documents | Unlimited |
| API calls | Unlimited |
| Storage | VPS disk |
| Cost | VPS only |

**Pro:** Truly unlimited everything. Zero per-project fees. Full data ownership.
**Con:** YOU maintain 25 instances. Patching, backups, uptime = your problem.

**25-app cost: €8–16/mo + your time (2-4 hrs/mo sysadmin)**

---

## The comparison table

| Provider | 25 apps monthly cost | Shared billing? | Free tier usable for 25 blogs? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sanity** | **$0** | No (but doesn't matter — free tier is huge) | ✅ Yes, comfortably |
| **Directus self-hosted** | **€8–16** | N/A (self-hosted) | ✅ Yes, unlimited |
| **ButterCMS** | **$1,775** | No | ❌ 50-post cap kills it |
| **DatoCMS** | **€1,135** | Partial (add projects to one account for €39 each) | ❌ 300-record cap kills it |
| **Storyblok** | **$2,475** | No | ❌ 1-user cap kills it |

## The honest answer to your question

**No provider gives you a shared org plan that's cheaper than Sanity's free tier at 25 projects.** The CMS industry charges per project/space/site — that's universal. The difference is:

- Sanity's free tier is so generous (20 seats, 10K docs, 100 GB, 1M CDN requests **per project**) that shared billing doesn't matter
- Every competitor's free tier is so restrictive that you're forced into paid plans within weeks
- Even the "shared billing" options (DatoCMS at €39/extra project) cost €1,000+/mo for 25 apps

## Final ranking for your factory

| Rank | Provider | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 🥇 | **Sanity free** | $0 for 25 apps, best DX with Next.js, generous limits, no credit card needed |
| 🥈 | **Directus self-hosted** | €8-16/mo, unlimited everything, full ownership, but you're the sysadmin |
| 🥉 | **Everything else** | $1,000+/mo — not designed for your use case |

**Sanity's competitive moat IS the free tier.** They give you unlimited projects for free because their business model is: start free → grow → one project eventually upgrades to Growth ($15/seat) → then Enterprise. They're betting that 2-3 of your 25 apps will eventually generate enough revenue to justify upgrading. The other 22 stay free forever and that's fine with them.

## Dataset Privacy Difference

On the free plan, private datasets are not available—if you don't add payment details and upgrade to the Growth plan, your project automatically downgrades to the free plan when the trial ends, and private datasets will become public.

Every new project automatically gets a free trial of the Growth Plan features, including private datasets, but with the same usage limits as the free plan.

## What This Means

The fundamental difference is:

- **Public datasets**: Only unauthenticated users or requests without authorization tokens can read from the dataset, and public datasets allow public read-only access, while write always requires a token with appropriate permissions.

- **Private datasets**: Only authenticated users or requests with authorization tokens can read from the dataset.

Here's what "public" and "private" means on that pricing page — it's about **datasets**, not plans.

## Public vs Private Dataset

It controls **who can READ your content without a login token.**

```
PUBLIC dataset (free plan)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Anyone who knows your project ID can READ   │
│ your content via the API. No token needed.  │
│                                             │
│ ✅ Read = open to the internet              │
│ 🔒 Write = still requires auth token        │
│ 🔒 Studio login = still requires account    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

PRIVATE dataset (Growth plan only, $15/seat/mo)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Nobody can read without a valid auth token. │
│ Every API call must include a secret token. │
│                                             │
│ 🔒 Read = requires token                   │
│ 🔒 Write = requires token                  │
│ 🔒 Studio login = requires account          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## What this means in practice

On the **free plan**, your datasets are public. That means:

```
# Anyone can do this if they know your project ID:
https://abc123.api.sanity.io/v2024-01-01/data/query/production?query=*[_type=="post"]

# Returns ALL your blog posts as JSON — titles, body, everything
# No token, no auth, just a URL
```

Your **project ID** is visible in your code (it's in the Sanity client config, which ships to the browser). So effectively, your blog content is publicly readable by anyone who inspects your frontend code.

## Does this matter for your use case?

**No. Here's why:**

| Content type | Publicly readable via dataset? | Already publicly readable on your website? | Risk? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blog posts | Yes | **Yes — they're on your public blog page** | ❌ None |
| Author bios | Yes | **Yes — shown on the blog** | ❌ None |
| Cover images | Yes | **Yes — rendered on the page** | ❌ None |
| Draft posts | Yes (prefixed with `drafts.`) | No — not shown on site until published | ⚠️ Minor |

The only real exposure is **draft posts** — someone could query your public dataset and see unpublished drafts. For a blog, this is negligible. Nobody is hunting for your draft blog posts.

## When private datasets actually matter

Private datasets are important for:

- **E-commerce** — product pricing, inventory, unreleased products
- **Internal tools** — employee data, internal docs
- **Gated content** — paid courses, member-only resources
- **Sensitive data** — anything you wouldn't put on a public webpage

**For a marketing blog, 100% of your content is already public on your website.** Making the dataset public just means the same data is also readable through the API — it changes nothing about your security posture.

## The free plan flow

```
You create a project → 30-day Growth trial starts (private datasets available)
                     → trial ends
                     → drops to free plan
                     → datasets become PUBLIC automatically
                     → your blog keeps working, nothing breaks
                     → the only change: API reads no longer need a token
```

**Don't build around private datasets during the trial.** They'll disappear when the trial ends. Start with the assumption that everything is public, and you'll never have a surprise.

## Summary

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| What is "public" on the pricing page? | Your data is readable via API without authentication |
| What is "private"? | Your data requires a token to read via API |
| Which do you get on free? | **Public only** |
| Does this affect your blog? | **No** — blog content is already public on your website |
| Can people edit/delete your content? | **No** — writes always require auth, even on public datasets |
| Can people see your drafts? | Technically yes, but nobody will bother |
| Should you pay for private? | **No** — not for marketing blogs. Save $15/seat/mo. |

**Public datasets on free plan = perfectly fine for your 25 marketing blogs.** This is a non-issue. Lock it in?

Here's the honest answer after checking every major headless CMS.

## The industry truth

**No headless CMS offers "one paid plan → covers all your projects."** Every single provider bills per project/space/repository. This is universal:

| Provider | Billing model | Shared org plan? |
|---|---|---|
| Sanity | Per project | ❌ |
| Contentful | Per space | ❌ (Enterprise custom quote only, $60K+/yr) |
| Storyblok | Per space | ❌ |
| Hygraph | Per project | ❌ |
| DatoCMS | Per project (€39/extra) | ❌ (closest, but still per-project add-on) |
| ButterCMS | Per site | ❌ |
| Prismic | Per repository | ❌ |
| Payload Cloud | Per project | ❌ |
| Strapi Cloud | Per project | ❌ |

**"Shared workspace across projects" simply doesn't exist in the headless CMS industry.** It's like asking for a hosting provider where one plan covers unlimited apps — nobody does it because each project consumes independent resources.

## But you have 2 workarounds

### Workaround 1: One Sanity project for ALL 25 apps (hacky but possible)

Instead of 25 separate projects, put everything in ONE project with prefixed content types:

```
Single Sanity project: "boldteq-factory"
├── boldteq_post       (Boldteq blog posts)
├── boldteq_author
├── pinzo_post         (Pinzo blog posts)  
├── pinzo_author
├── rankora_post       (Rankora blog posts)
├── rankora_author
├── ... × 25 apps
```

Each Next.js app queries only its own prefixed types:

```ts
// Boldteq marketing site
sanityClient.fetch(`*[_type == "boldteq_post"]`)

// Pinzo marketing site  
sanityClient.fetch(`*[_type == "pinzo_post"]`)
```

**Shared limits across all 25 apps:**

| Resource | Free tier total | Per app (÷25) | Enough? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Documents | 10,000 | 400 posts | ✅ For blog-only |
| Seats | 20 | Shared pool | ✅ You + a few editors |
| CDN requests | 1,000,000/mo | 40,000/app | ✅ With ISR |
| Bandwidth | 100 GB/mo | 4 GB/app | ✅ With next/image |
| Storage | 100 GB | 4 GB/app | ✅ |
| Webhooks | 2 | Shared | ⚠️ Tight — need custom routing |

**Pros:**
- One project, one Studio, one login, one bill ($0)
- Shared seat pool — your 2 editors have access to all 25 apps' content
- Never worry about per-project billing

**Cons:**
- Studio gets cluttered with 50+ content types
- One misconfiguration or schema error affects ALL 25 apps
- If you hit the 10K document limit, ALL apps are blocked
- Security blast radius — one compromised token = all apps exposed
- Webhook routing gets complex (which Next.js app to revalidate?)
- Harder to hand off or sell an individual app later (content is tangled)

**My take:** Works for 5 apps. Gets painful at 10. Unmanageable at 25.

### Workaround 2: Prismic free (unlimited docs, per-repo but very generous)

Prismic's free tier is interesting for your case:

| Resource | Prismic free (per repo) |
|---|---|
| Documents | **Unlimited** |
| API calls | **4,000,000/mo** |
| Users | 1 |
| Custom types | 25 |
| Locales | Limited (recent change) |

**The catch:** Only **1 user** on free. That means only you can edit. If you need a second editor, you're on the Starter plan ($10/repo/month). For 25 repos with 2 editors: $250/mo.

But if you're truly solo (just you + AI agents writing content), 25 Prismic free repos = **$0/mo with unlimited documents per repo.**

---

## The real comparison for "cheapest way to run 25 blogs"

| Approach | Monthly cost | Docs per app | Users per app | Maintenance | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **25 Sanity free projects** | **$0** | 10,000 | 20 | Zero | Vendor pricing change |
| **1 Sanity project, shared** | **$0** | ~400 (shared 10K) | 20 (shared) | Zero | Cluttered, fragile, tangled |
| **25 Prismic free repos** | **$0** | **Unlimited** | **1 only** | Zero | Need paid for 2nd user |
| **Directus self-hosted × 25** | **€8–16** | Unlimited | Unlimited | 2-4 hrs/mo | VPS management |
| **Keystatic × 25** (git-backed) | **$0** | Unlimited | Unlimited (GitHub) | ~Zero | No traditional CMS UI |

## My final honest recommendation

**There is no magic "shared workspace" CMS.** But you don't need one, because Sanity's free tier already gives you what shared billing would give: **$0 for all 25 apps.**

The "shared" options either:
- **Save nothing** (Sanity is already free per project)
- **Introduce worse problems** (tangled content in one project, 1-user caps, or sysadmin burden)

Here's the decision matrix:

| If you want... | Use |
|---|---|
| Best DX + generous free + zero maintenance | **25 Sanity free projects** (recommended) |
| Truly unlimited docs + solo editing only | **25 Prismic free repos** |
| Full control + unlimited everything | **Directus self-hosted on Coolify** |
| Zero vendor dependency at all | **Keystatic** (markdown in git) |
| One shared workspace for all apps | **Doesn't exist.** Closest = one Sanity project with prefixed types (not recommended at 25 apps) |

---

**Bottom line: "shared workspace" is a feature that doesn't exist in this industry. But it doesn't matter — Sanity free × 25 projects costs $0 and gives you 20 seats + 10K docs + 100 GB per app independently. That's better than any shared plan would be.**
